claim: Bub1 and BubR1 are SAC components that originated from duplication of an ancestor gene.
source: Bub1 and BubR1, SAC components, originated from duplication of an ancestor gene.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by citation to previous work (Suijkerbuijk et al., 2012a) in the introduction.

claim: Subsequent sub-functionalization established subordination where Bub1, recruited first to kinetochores, promotes successive BubR1 recruitment.
source: Subsequent sub-functionalization established subordination: Bub1, recruited first to kinetochores, promotes successive BubR1 recruitment.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is a central finding of the study.

claim: Both Bub1 and BubR1 hetero-dimerize with Bub3, a targeting adaptor for phosphorylated kinetochores.
source: Because both Bub1 and BubR1 hetero-dimerize with Bub3, a targeting adaptor for phosphorylated kinetochores, the molecular basis for such sub-functionalization is unclear.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data and citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Bub1, but not BubR1, enhances binding of Bub3 to phosphorylated kinetochores.
source: We demonstrate that Bub1, but not BubR1, enhances binding of Bub3 to phosphorylated kinetochores.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated experimentally in Figure 2A.

claim: Grafting a short motif of Bub1 onto BubR1 promotes Bub1-independent kinetochore recruitment of BubR1.
source: Grafting a short motif of Bub1 onto BubR1 promotes Bub1-independent kinetochore recruitment of BubR1.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 3E-F.

claim: The gain-of-function BubR1 mutant (with Bub1 loop) cannot sustain a functional checkpoint.
source: This gain-of-function BubR1 mutant cannot sustain a functional checkpoint.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 3I.

claim: Kinetochore localization of BubR1 relies on direct hetero-dimerization with Bub1 at a pseudo-symmetric interface.
source: We demonstrate that kinetochore localization of BubR1 relies on direct hetero-dimerization with Bub1 at a pseudo-symmetric interface.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through size exclusion chromatography experiments in Figures 4-6.

claim: The pseudo-symmetric interaction underpins a template–copy relationship crucial for kinetochore–microtubule attachment and SAC signaling.
source: This pseudo-symmetric interaction underpins a template–copy relationship crucial for kinetochore–microtubule attachment and SAC signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and discussed extensively in the Discussion section with reference to the Mad1/Mad2 template-copy mechanism.

claim: Bub1 and BubR1 originated from a gene that was already present in the hypothetical last eukaryotic common ancestor (LECA).
source: Bub1 and BubR1 originated from a gene that was already present in the hypothetical last eukaryotic common ancestor (LECA) (Suijkerbuijk et al., 2012a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to Suijkerbuijk et al., 2012a.

claim: Up to nine distinct duplication events of the Bub1/BubR1 ancestor gene might have occurred after speciation.
source: After speciation, up to nine distinct duplication events might have occurred, which invariably led to sub-functionalization of the resulting gene products (Suijkerbuijk et al., 2012a).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to Suijkerbuijk et al., 2012a.

claim: Human Bub1 and BubR1 are strongly conserved at the sequence and domain level.
source: Human Bub1 and BubR1 are strongly conserved at the sequence and domain level (Figure 1A) but play complementary roles in the SAC.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and illustrated in Figure 1A showing similar domain organization.

claim: Bub1 becomes recruited to kinetochores in prometaphase to provide a platform for additional SAC proteins, including Mad1, Mad2, the BubR1/Bub3 complex, and Cdc20.
source: Bub1 becomes recruited to kinetochores in prometaphase to provide a platform for additional SAC proteins, including Mad1, Mad2, the BubR1/Bub3 complex, and Cdc20.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations (Lara-Gonzalez et al., 2012; Foley and Kapoor, 2013).

claim: Bub1 promotes the assembly of Mad2, BubR1/Bub3, and Cdc20 into the mitotic checkpoint complex (MCC).
source: Bub1 promotes the assembly of a subset of these proteins, Mad2, BubR1/Bub3, and Cdc20, into the SAC effector, the mitotic checkpoint complex (MCC), which targets the anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C) to inhibit its ability to promote mitotic exit (Lara-Gonzalez et al., 2012; Foley and Kapoor, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Bub1 kinase activity is not required for the SAC.
source: Bub1 kinase activity is not required for the SAC (Sharp-Baker and Chen, 2001; Fernius and Hardwick, 2007; Perera et al., 2007; Klebig et al., 2009) but contributes to stable kinetochore–microtubule attachments through phosphorylation of histone H2A on Thr120 and subsequent localization of Sgo1 to centromeres and kinetochores (Kawashima et al., 2010; Wang et al., 2011; Caldas et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations.

claim: BubR1 evolved into an inactive pseudo-kinase.
source: BubR1, on the other hand, evolved into an inactive pseudo-kinase (Suijkerbuijk et al., 2012a) and is a crucial subunit of the MCC (Hardwick et al., 2000; Fraschini et al., 2001; Sudakin et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to Suijkerbuijk et al., 2012a.

claim: BubR1 is a crucial subunit of the MCC.
source: BubR1, on the other hand, evolved into an inactive pseudo-kinase (Suijkerbuijk et al., 2012a) and is a crucial subunit of the MCC (Hardwick et al., 2000; Fraschini et al., 2001; Sudakin et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: BubR1 contributes to the formation of stable kinetochore–microtubule attachments and checkpoint silencing through kinetochore co-recruitment of protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A).
source: BubR1 contributes to the formation of stable kinetochore–microtubule attachments and checkpoint silencing through kinetochore co-recruitment of protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) (Suijkerbuijk et al., 2012b; Kruse et al., 2013; Xu et al., 2013; Espert et al., 2014; Nijenhuis et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations.

claim: Bub1 interacts stably with unattached kinetochores.
source: Bub1 interacts stably with unattached kinetochores, in agreement with its function as a SAC recruitment platform, while BubR1 turns over rapidly (t1/2 = 3–20 s), likely reflecting its cycle of incorporation into MCC and its release into the cytosol as a soluble APC/C inhibitor (Howell et al., 2004; Shah et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: BubR1 turns over rapidly at kinetochores (t1/2 = 3–20 s).
source: Bub1 interacts stably with unattached kinetochores, in agreement with its function as a SAC recruitment platform, while BubR1 turns over rapidly (t1/2 = 3–20 s), likely reflecting its cycle of incorporation into MCC and its release into the cytosol as a soluble APC/C inhibitor (Howell et al., 2004; Shah et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Kinetochore recruitment of Bub1 is independent of BubR1.
source: Besides different dynamics, another important difference is that kinetochore recruitment of Bub1 is independent of BubR1, while recruitment of BubR1 is strictly subordinate to Bub1 (Millband and Hardwick, 2002; Gillett et al., 2004; Johnson et al., 2004; Perera et al., 2007; Logarinho et al., 2008; Klebig et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations and confirmed experimentally in Figure 1E-F.

claim: Recruitment of BubR1 is strictly subordinate to Bub1.
source: Besides different dynamics, another important difference is that kinetochore recruitment of Bub1 is independent of BubR1, while recruitment of BubR1 is strictly subordinate to Bub1 (Millband and Hardwick, 2002; Gillett et al., 2004; Johnson et al., 2004; Perera et al., 2007; Logarinho et al., 2008; Klebig et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations and confirmed experimentally in Figure 1G-H.

claim: Bub3 targets kinetochores by binding to phosphorylated Met-Glu-Leu-ThrP (MELTP) repeats of the outer kinetochore subunit Knl1.
source: Bub3 is a 7-WD40 β-propeller that targets kinetochores by binding to phosphorylated Met-Glu-Leu-ThrP (MELTP, where TP indicates phosphothreonine) repeats of the outer kinetochore subunit Knl1 (a.k.a. Casc5, Spc105, Spc7, AF15q14, and Blinkin) (Kiyomitsu et al., 2007; Krenn et al., 2012, 2014; London et al., 2012; Shepperd et al., 2012; Yamagishi et al., 2012; Primorac et al., 2013) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations.

claim: Bub3 binds tightly to Bub1 and BubR1 via conserved segments known as Bub3-binding domain (B3BD) or GLEBS.
source: Bub3 binds tightly to Bub1 and BubR1 via conserved segments known as Bub3-binding domain (B3BD) or GLEBS (Taylor et al., 1998; Larsen et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: Bub3 co-recruits Bub1 to kinetochores in Saccharomyces cerevisiae by recognizing MELTP.
source: By recognizing MELTP, Bub3 co-recruits Bub1 to kinetochores in Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Primorac et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citation to Primorac et al., 2013.

claim: In human cells, Bub3 is required for kinetochore recruitment of Bub1 and BubR1.
source: In human cells, Bub3 is required for kinetochore recruitment of Bub1 and BubR1, and consistently the B3BDs of Bub1 and BubR1 are necessary, and in the case of Bub1 also sufficient, for kinetochore targeting of Bub1 and BubR1 (Taylor et al., 1998; Logarinho et al., 2008; Malureanu et al., 2009; Elowe et al., 2010; Lara-Gonzalez et al., 2011; Krenn et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations.

claim: The B3BD of Bub1 is sufficient for kinetochore targeting of Bub1.
source: In human cells, Bub3 is required for kinetochore recruitment of Bub1 and BubR1, and consistently the B3BDs of Bub1 and BubR1 are necessary, and in the case of Bub1 also sufficient, for kinetochore targeting of Bub1 and BubR1 (Taylor et al., 1998; Logarinho et al., 2008; Malureanu et al., 2009; Elowe et al., 2010; Lara-Gonzalez et al., 2011; Krenn et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations and confirmed experimentally in Figure 1I.

claim: Mps1 phosphorylates MELT repeats of Knl1 to promote kinetochore recruitment of Bub1 and BubR1.
source: The SAC kinase Mps1 has been shown to phosphorylate MELT repeats of Knl1 to promote kinetochore recruitment of Bub1 and BubR1 (Heinrich et al., 2012; London et al., 2012; Shepperd et al., 2012; Yamagishi et al., 2012; Primorac et al., 2013; Vleugel et al., 2013; Krenn et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with multiple citations and confirmed by mass spectrometry in Figure 1C-D.

claim: Inhibition of Mps1 with Reversine strongly suppresses the interaction of Bub1, BubR1, and Bub3 with kinetochores.
source: Quantitative mass spectrometry (see 'Materials and methods') of proteins associated with Bub1 or Knl1 confirmed the crucial role of Mps1, as we observed a strong suppression of the interaction of Bub1, BubR1, and Bub3 with kinetochores in the presence of Reversine (Figure 1C–D. Large deviations from a value of 1 for the Reversine/DMSO ratio indicate suppression of binding).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and demonstrated in Figure 1C-D.

claim: Bub1 decorated kinetochores at essentially normal levels after the depletion of BubR1.
source: In HeLa cells treated with nocodazole, which depolymerizes microtubules and activates the SAC, Bub1 decorated kinetochores at essentially normal levels after the depletion of BubR1 (Figure 1E, quantified in Figure 1F. Quantifications of RNAi-based depletions are shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1E-F.

claim: BubR1 did not decorate kinetochores after Bub1 depletion.
source: Conversely, BubR1 did not decorate kinetochores after Bub1 depletion (Figure 1G–H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1G-H.

claim: Bub1209-270, encompassing the B3BD, is the minimal Bub1 localization domain.
source: By monitoring the localization of a GFP-Bub1 reporter construct, we had previously demonstrated that Bub1209-270, encompassing the B3BD, is the minimal Bub1 localization domain (Taylor et al., 1998; Krenn et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: Bub1209–270 targeted kinetochores very efficiently even after the depletion of endogenous Bub1.
source: Bub1209–270 targeted kinetochores very efficiently even after the depletion of endogenous Bub1 (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1I.

claim: BubR1362–431 was not recruited to kinetochores even in the presence of Bub1.
source: BubR1362–431 was not recruited to kinetochores even in the presence of Bub1 (Figure 1J. Diagrams of Bub1 and BubR1 deletions used in this study are in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1J.

claim: The B3BD of Bub1 strongly enhanced binding of Bub3 to phosphorylated MBP-Knl1MELT1 but not to unphosphorylated MBP-Knl1MELT1.
source: The B3BD of Bub1 strongly enhanced binding of Bub3 to phosphorylated MBP-Knl1MELT1 but not to unphosphorylated MBP-Knl1MELT1, while the B3BD of BubR1 had a negligible effect (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The B3BD of BubR1 had a negligible effect on binding of Bub3 to phosphorylated MBP-Knl1MELT1.
source: The B3BD of Bub1 strongly enhanced binding of Bub3 to phosphorylated MBP-Knl1MELT1 but not to unphosphorylated MBP-Knl1MELT1, while the B3BD of BubR1 had a negligible effect (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Bub3 in isolation did not bind MBP-Knl1MELT1.
source: Bub3 in isolation did not bind MBP-Knl1MELT1, in agreement with our previous data (Krenn et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citation and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The 'loop' region of Bub1 or BubR1 is between strands β1 and β2 and precedes the highly conserved core of the B3BD.
source: The 'loop' region of Bub1 or BubR1 is between strands β1 and β2 (Figure 2B–D) and precedes the highly conserved core of the B3BD.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and illustrated in Figure 2B-D.

claim: The loop abuts the binding site for the MELTP peptide and is ideally positioned to modulate the binding affinity of Bub3 for MELTP.
source: The loop abuts the binding site for the MELTP peptide and is therefore ideally positioned to modulate the binding affinity of Bub3 for MELTP (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and illustrated in Figure 2C-D.

claim: Bub1209–270/BR1-loop bound weakly to phosphorylated MBP-Knl1MELT1.
source: Bub1209–270 bound tightly and in an Mps1-phosphorylation-dependent manner to MBP-Knl1MELT1 (Figure 2F), while Bub1209–270/BR1–loop bound weakly.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: BubR1362–431/B1–loop bound more strongly to phosphorylated MBP-Knl1MELT1 than did BubR1362–431.
source: Conversely, BubR1362–431/B1–loop bound more strongly to phosphorylated MBP-Knl1MELT1 than did BubR1362–431 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Loop swap mutants interacted with Bub3 as efficiently as wild-type counterparts.
source: Loop swap mutants interacted with Bub3 as efficiently as wild-type counterparts, but the interactions that Bub3 mediates, most notably those with the Knl1 receptor and its associated partner Mis12, were strongly enhanced when the Bub1 loop region was grafted onto BubR1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2G-H.

claim: The interactions that Bub3 mediates with the Knl1 receptor and Mis12 were strongly enhanced when the Bub1 loop region was grafted onto BubR1.
source: Loop swap mutants interacted with Bub3 as efficiently as wild-type counterparts, but the interactions that Bub3 mediates, most notably those with the Knl1 receptor and its associated partner Mis12, were strongly enhanced when the Bub1 loop region was grafted onto BubR1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2G-H.

claim: Kinetochore localization of GFP-Bub1BR1–loop was weaker than that of wild-type Bub1.
source: Kinetochore localization of GFP-Bub1BR1–loop was weaker than that of wild-type Bub1 (Figure 3A–B), whereas kinetochore localization of GFP-BubR1B1–loop was stronger than that of unmodified BubR1 (Figure 3C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A-B.

claim: Kinetochore localization of GFP-BubR1B1–loop was stronger than that of unmodified BubR1.
source: Kinetochore localization of GFP-Bub1BR1–loop was weaker than that of wild-type Bub1 (Figure 3A–B), whereas kinetochore localization of GFP-BubR1B1–loop was stronger than that of unmodified BubR1 (Figure 3C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3C-D.

claim: GFP-BubR1B1–loop decorated kinetochores even after the depletion of Bub1.
source: Indeed, GFP-BubR1B1–loop decorated kinetochores even after the depletion of Bub1. Thus, when grafted onto BubR1, the Bub1 loop region is sufficient to confer upon BubR1 the ability to target kinetochores in a Bub1-independent fashion (Figure 3E–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3E-F.

claim: Kinetochore localization of GFP-BubR1B1–loop in cells depleted of Bub1 was inhibited by addition of Reversine.
source: Kinetochore localization of GFP-BubR1B1–loop in cells depleted of Bub1 was inhibited by addition of Reversine, indicating a dependence on Mps1 and MELTP sequences (Figure 3G–H and Figure 3—figure supplement 1, panel A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3G-H.

claim: Expression of BubR1B1–loop did not overtly affect the kinetochore levels of endogenous Bub1.
source: Expression of BubR1B1–loop did not overtly affect the kinetochore levels of endogenous Bub1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, panel B), suggesting that the multiple MELTP sequences of Knl1 are not saturated with endogenous Bub1 even in the strong checkpoint-activating conditions of our assay.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1, panel B.

claim: In cells depleted of endogenous BubR1, wild-type BubR1 restored SAC function to a high degree but GFP-BubR1B1–loop failed to do so.
source: In cells depleted of endogenous BubR1, wild-type BubR1 restored SAC function to a high degree but GFP-BubR1B1–loop failed to do so (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3I.

claim: GFP-BubR1B1–loop showed much less association with MCC and APC/C subunits compared to GFP-BubR1.
source: Comparison of immune-precipitates of GFP-BubR1 and GFP-BubR1B1–loop from nocodazole-treated mitotic cells showed much less of the latter associated with MCC and APC/C subunits (Figure 3J, quantified in Figure 3—figure supplement 1, panel C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3J.

claim: Immune-precipitation of the APC/C demonstrated association of GFP-BubR1, but not GFP-BubR1B1–loop, with the APC/C.
source: Similarly, immune-precipitation (IP) of the APC/C demonstrated association of GFP-BubR1, but not GFP-BubR1B1–loop, with the APC/C (Figure 3K, quantified in Figure 3—figure supplement 1, panel D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3K.

claim: Bub1209–270, encompassing the B3BD and localizing robustly to kinetochores, did not recruit BubR1 in cells depleted of endogenous Bub1.
source: Bub1209–270, encompassing the B3BD and localizing robustly to kinetochores, did not recruit BubR1 in cells depleted of endogenous Bub1 (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: Bub11–284, containing the tetratrico peptide repeats (TPRs) and the B3BD of Bub1, targeted kinetochores but did not recruit BubR1.
source: A construct containing the tetratrico peptide repeats (TPRs) and the B3BD of Bub1, Bub11–284, also targeted kinetochores but did not recruit BubR1 (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: Bub1209–409, consisting of the B3BD and a ∼140-residue C-terminal extension (CTE), targeted kinetochores and promoted robust kinetochore localization of BubR1.
source: On the contrary, a segment (Bub1209–409) consisting of the B3BD and a ∼140-residue C-terminal extension (CTE), targeted kinetochores and promoted robust kinetochore localization of BubR1 (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: Bub1 does not require the CTE (residues 271–409) for its own kinetochore recruitment but requires it to recruit BubR1.
source: Thus, Bub1 does not require the CTE (residues 271–409) for its own kinetochore recruitment (the B3BD, residues 209–270, is sufficient) but requires it to recruit BubR1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4A-D.

claim: Bub1Δ271–409 targeted kinetochores efficiently but failed to recruit BubR1.
source: A deletion mutant lacking the CTE (Bub1Δ271–409) targeted kinetochores efficiently but failed to recruit BubR1 (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4C-D.

claim: GFP-Bub1209–409 interacted with BubR1 at levels that were only modestly lower than those of full-length GFP-Bub1.
source: In IP experiments both in the presence and absence of endogenous Bub1, GFP-Bub1209–409 interacted with BubR1 at levels that were only modestly lower than those of full-length GFP-Bub1 (Figure 4E–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4E-F.

claim: GFP-Bub1209–270 did not interact with BubR1.
source: Conversely, GFP-Bub1209–270 did not interact with BubR1, in agreement with the inability of this construct to promote BubR1 localization.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4E-F.

claim: Bub11–409 and BubR11–571 bind directly in size-exclusion chromatography experiments.
source: In size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) experiments, in which the elution volume reflects macromolecular mass and shape, BubR11–571/Bub3 bound stoichiometrically to Bub11–409/Bub3 (Figure 4G), thus demonstrating a direct interaction in the absence of other proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4G.

claim: BubR11–571 did not require Bub3 to bind Bub11–409/Bub3 in vitro.
source: In these experiments in vitro, BubR11–571 did not require Bub3 to bind Bub11–409/Bub3 (Figure 4H), and therefore in the following SEC experiments, we used BubR1 and BubR1/Bub3 interchangeably (whereas Bub1 was poorly expressed and largely insoluble in insect cells without Bub3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Bub1209–409/Bub3 formed a stoichiometric complex with BubR11–571/Bub3.
source: In agreement with the ability of Bub1209–409 to recruit BubR1 to kinetochores, Bub1209–409/Bub3 formed a stoichiometric complex with BubR11–571/Bub3 (Figure 4I) or BubR11–571 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, panel A), further showing that the Bub1 TPR region is dispensable.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Neither the isolated B3BD of Bub1 (Bub1209–270/Bub3) nor the isolated CTE (Bub1271–409) bound BubR11–571/Bub3.
source: Neither the isolated B3BD of Bub1 (Bub1209–270/Bub3, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B) nor the isolated CTE (Bub1271–409, Figure 4J) bound BubR11–571/Bub3, indicating that both regions contribute to BubR1 binding in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4J and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: BubR1362–571, which contains the B3BD and a ∼140-residue CTE, localized to kinetochores in a Bub1-dependent manner.
source: BubR1362–571, which contains the B3BD and a ∼140-residue CTE, localized to kinetochores in a Bub1-dependent manner (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5A-B.

claim: Shorter fragments of BubR1, including the isolated B3BD (BubR1362–431) and the isolated CTE (BubR1432–571), did not localize to kinetochores.
source: Shorter fragments of BubR1, including the isolated B3BD (BubR1362–431, see also Figure 1J) and the isolated CTE (BubR1432–571), did not localize to kinetochores (Figure 5B–C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5B-C.

claim: BubR1362–571 bound to Bub11–409/Bub3 in SEC experiments.
source: In agreement with the kinetochore recruitment assay, SEC experiments showed binding of BubR1362–571 but not of the isolated B3BD (BubR1362–431/Bub3) or the isolated CTE (BubR1432–571) to Bub11–409/Bub3 (Figure 5D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The isolated B3BD (BubR1362–431/Bub3) did not bind to Bub11–409/Bub3 in SEC experiments.
source: In agreement with the kinetochore recruitment assay, SEC experiments showed binding of BubR1362–571 but not of the isolated B3BD (BubR1362–431/Bub3) or the isolated CTE (BubR1432–571) to Bub11–409/Bub3 (Figure 5D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The isolated CTE (BubR1432–571) did not bind to Bub11–409/Bub3 in SEC experiments.
source: In agreement with the kinetochore recruitment assay, SEC experiments showed binding of BubR1362–571 but not of the isolated B3BD (BubR1362–431/Bub3) or the isolated CTE (BubR1432–571) to Bub11–409/Bub3 (Figure 5D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The sequences of Bub1209–409 and BubR1362–571 are structurally equivalent.
source: An alignment of the interacting domains of Bub1 and BubR1 (residues 209–409 and 362–571, respectively; the alignment was obtained with programs Muscle [Edgar, 2004] and JPRED [Cole et al., 2008]) shows that their sequences are structurally equivalent (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The ability of modern-day Bub1 and BubR1 to form heterodimers using structurally equivalent segments may reflect the ability of their ancestor to form homodimers.
source: We surmise that the ability of modern-day Bub1 and BubR1 to form heterodimers using these structurally equivalent ('pseudo-symmetric') segments may reflect the ability of their ancestor to form homodimers, similarly to what is observed in cohesins.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a speculation based on the structural equivalence.

claim: Deletion of residues 432–484 of BubR1 (GFP-BubR1Δ432–484) in the predicted helical region impaired kinetochore localization of BubR1.
source: Deletion of residues 432–484 of BubR1 (GFP-BubR1Δ432–484) in the predicted helical region impaired kinetochore localization of BubR1 (Figure 6C–D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6C-D.

claim: Mutations in the B3BD of BubR1 (E409K + E413K) known to impair Bub3 binding prevented kinetochore localization of full-length BubR1.
source: Additionally, mutations in the B3BD of BubR1 (E409K + E413K) known to impair Bub3 binding (Taylor et al., 1998; Larsen et al., 2007) prevented kinetochore localization of full-length BubR1 (Figure 6E–F) and of BubR1362–571 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1, panels B–C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6E-F.

claim: Bub3 binding is necessary for efficient kinetochore localization of BubR1.
source: Thus, Bub3 binding is necessary for efficient kinetochore localization of BubR1 even if it may appear to be dispensable for the interaction in vitro (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on the E409K+E413K mutant data.

claim: LacI-Bub1 recruited BubR1 to an ectopic LacO site distinct from centromeres.
source: To try distinguishing between these possibilities, we targeted a Lac repressor (LacI) fusion of Bub1 to an ectopic Lac operator (LacO) site on the chromosome distinct from centromeres. LacI-Bub1 recruited BubR1 to the ectopic site (Figure 6G–H, quantified in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), thus suggesting that kinetochores are not required for the Bub1/BubR1 interaction, in agreement with a previous study in Schizosaccharomyces pombe (Rischitor et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6G-H.

claim: Mutation of the Bub3-binding site of the LacI-Bub1 fusion (Bub1E252K) prevented BubR1 recruitment.
source: Mutation of the Bub3-binding site of the LacI-Bub1 fusion (Bub1E252K) prevented BubR1 recruitment, suggesting that Bub3 is required for a robust interaction between Bub1 and BubR1 on both sides of the complex (Figure 6G–H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6G-H.

claim: HeLa cells depleted of endogenous BubR1 failed to arrest in mitosis in the presence of nocodazole.
source: HeLa cells depleted of endogenous BubR1 failed to arrest in mitosis in the presence of nocodazole (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: SAC proficiency was re-established upon expression of GFP-BubR1 but not GFP-BubR1E409K+E413K.
source: SAC proficiency was re-established upon expression of GFP-BubR1 but not GFP-BubR1E409K+E413K.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: GFP-BubR1Δ432–484 restored a robust SAC response.
source: GFP-BubR1Δ432–484, on the other hand, restored a robust SAC response.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: GFP-BubR1E409K+E413K was unable to interact with Bub1 or Knl1.
source: IP experiments indicated that both GFP-BubR1E409K+E413K and GFP-BubR1Δ432–484 were unable to interact with Bub1 or Knl1, as expected based on their localization behavior.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7B.

claim: GFP-BubR1Δ432–484 was unable to interact with Bub1 or Knl1.
source: IP experiments indicated that both GFP-BubR1E409K+E413K and GFP-BubR1Δ432–484 were unable to interact with Bub1 or Knl1, as expected based on their localization behavior.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7B.

claim: GFP-BubR1E409K+E413K was significantly impaired in its ability to interact with Mad2 and Cdc20.
source: However, GFP-BubR1E409K+E413K was also significantly impaired in its ability to interact with two additional MCC subunits (Mad2 and Cdc20) and was even more dramatically impaired in its ability to interact with the APC/C.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7B.

claim: GFP-BubR1E409K+E413K was dramatically impaired in its ability to interact with the APC/C.
source: However, GFP-BubR1E409K+E413K was also significantly impaired in its ability to interact with two additional MCC subunits (Mad2 and Cdc20) and was even more dramatically impaired in its ability to interact with the APC/C.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7B.

claim: GFP-BubR1Δ432–484 interacted with the MCC subunits and with the APC/C at levels that were comparable to those of the wild-type GFP-BubR1 control.
source: Conversely, GFP-BubR1Δ432–484 interacted with the MCC subunits (including Bub3, as expected) and with the APC/C at levels that were comparable to those of the wild-type GFP-BubR1 control (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7B.

claim: BubR1 needs to bind Bub3 to become incorporated into the MCC in human cells.
source: On the other hand, because GFP-BubR1E409K+E413K does not bind Bub3, while GFP-BubR1Δ432–484 does (Figure 7B, quantified in Figure 7C), it appears that at least in human cells BubR1 needs to bind Bub3 to become incorporated into the MCC.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on comparison of the two mutants.

claim: Both GFP-BubR1E409K+E413K and GFP-BubR1Δ432–484 failed to complement the deficits in promoting the formation of stable kinetochore–microtubule attachments observed in cells depleted of endogenous BubR1.
source: Both GFP-BubR1E409K+E413K and GFP-BubR1Δ432–484, neither of which localizes to kinetochores, failed to complement the deficits in promoting the formation of stable kinetochore–microtubule attachments observed in cells depleted of endogenous BubR1 (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The role of BubR1 in kinetochore–microtubule attachment has been attributed to its interaction with the B56 regulatory subunit of PP2AB56.
source: The role of BubR1 in kinetochore–microtubule attachment has been attributed to its interaction with the B56 regulatory subunit of a complex of protein phosphatase 2A (PP2AB56) (Suijkerbuijk et al., 2012b; Kruse et al., 2013; Xu et al., 2013; Espert et al., 2014; Nijenhuis et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with multiple citations.

claim: The levels of the B56 regulatory subunit in IPs of the GFP-BubR1Δ432–484 mutant were much lower than those of the wild-type protein.
source: We asked if the defect of the BubR1Δ432–484 mutant in supporting kinetochore–microtubule attachment correlated with a defective interaction with PP2AB56. Indeed, the levels of the B56 regulatory subunit in IPs of the GFP-BubR1Δ432–484 mutant were much lower than those of the wild-type protein (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The duplication of an ancestor gene and subsequent divergence was exploited during evolution to create Bub1 and BubR1 with highly diversified and efficient functions.
source: Our analysis of the mechanism of recruitment of Bub1 and BubR1 illustrates how the duplication of an ancestor gene and subsequent divergence was exploited during evolution to create two gene products with highly diversified and efficient functions, including monitoring checkpoint status through stable recruitment to unattached kinetochores (Bub1), effecting APC/C inhibition through incorporation into the MCC (BubR1), stabilization of microtubule attachment (Bub1 and BubR1, possibly through different mechanisms), and SAC silencing (BubR1).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of the findings.

claim: The occurrence of nine distinct duplications of the Bub1 and BubR1 ancestor likely reflects an extreme evolutionary pressure to separate functions that were originally condensed in a single gene.
source: The occurrence of nine distinct duplications of the Bub1 and BubR1 ancestor (Suijkerbuijk et al., 2012a) likely reflects an extreme evolutionary pressure to separate functions that were originally condensed in a single gene.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the evolutionary data.

claim: The loss of kinase activity specifically in BubR1 but not Bub1 was identified as a manifestation of the divergence of these proteins.
source: Previously, the loss of kinase activity specifically in BubR1 but not Bub1 was identified as a manifestation of the divergence of these proteins (Vleugel et al., 2012; Suijkerbuijk et al., 2012b).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: A suboptimal loop region for MELTP binding in BubR1 makes it depend on an alternative mechanism for kinetochore localization, which is the direct interaction with Bub1.
source: A suboptimal loop region for MELTP binding in BubR1 makes it depend on an alternative mechanism for kinetochore localization. This alternative is the direct interaction with Bub1, extensively characterized in Figures 4–6.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of the findings.

claim: The failure of the BubR1 gain-of-function mutant to complement the depletion of wild-type BubR1 strongly suggests that the evolutionary divergence of Bub1 and BubR1 is functionally relevant.
source: The failure of the BubR1 gain-of-function mutant to complement the depletion of wild-type BubR1 strongly suggests that the evolutionary divergence of Bub1 and BubR1, with its specific effects on kinetochore recruitment, is functionally relevant.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the data in Figure 3I.

claim: Bub3 has at least three distinct functions: (1) it recruits Bub1 to MELTP motifs of Knl1; (2) it contributes to the dimerization of Bub1 with BubR1 required for kinetochore recruitment of the latter; and (3) in complex with BubR1, it has an additional hitherto unknown function in the SAC.
source: Thus, Bub3 has at least three distinct functions: (1) it recruits Bub1 to MELTP motifs of Knl1; (2) it contributes to the dimerization of Bub1 with BubR1 required for kinetochore recruitment of the latter; and (3) in complex with BubR1, it has an additional hitherto unknown function in the SAC.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of Bub3 functions.

claim: The SAC defect observed with the BubR1E409K+E413K mutant is unlikely to be a consequence of impaired kinetochore localization.
source: The SAC defect observed with this mutant is unlikely to be a consequence of impaired kinetochore localization, because another kinetochore-localization impaired mutant, BubR1Δ432–484, was checkpoint proficient.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on comparison of the two mutants.

claim: BubR1-bound Bub3 is involved in an unknown aspect of the SAC mechanism downstream of kinetochores, possibly having to do with MCC formation or APC/C binding.
source: We surmise that BubR1-bound Bub3 is involved in an unknown aspect of the SAC mechanism downstream of kinetochores, possibly having to do with MCC formation or APC/C binding, as recently proposed (Han et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation based on the data.

claim: The BubR1 loop motif influences the specificity of BubR1-bound Bub3 for additional SAC-relevant targets.
source: In analogy with the role of the Bub1 loop motif in modulating the function of Bub3 as a MELTP receptor, we speculate that the BubR1 loop motif influences the specificity of BubR1-bound Bub3 for additional SAC-relevant targets.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation.

claim: The fact that the 'loop swap' BubR1 mutant is unable to sustain the SAC provides evidence for the hypothesis that the BubR1 loop motif influences Bub3 specificity.
source: The fact that the 'loop swap' BubR1 mutant is unable to sustain the SAC provides evidence for this hypothesis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the data in Figure 3I.

claim: Recruitment of PP2AB56 by BubR1 has been recently implicated in SAC silencing through a mechanism ultimately impinging on dephosphorylation of the MELTP motifs.
source: Recruitment of PP2AB56 by BubR1 has been recently implicated in SAC silencing through a mechanism ultimately impinging on dephosphorylation of the MELTP motifs (Espert et al., 2014; Nijenhuis et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: BubR1 promotes bi-orientation through recruitment of PP2AB56, which counteracts Aurora B activity and thus stabilizes kinetochore–microtubule attachments.
source: Previously, it has been shown that BubR1 promotes bi-orientation through recruitment of PP2AB56 (Suijkerbuijk et al., 2012b; Kruse et al., 2013; Xu et al., 2013), which counteracts Aurora B activity and thus stabilizes kinetochore–microtubule attachments (Lampson and Kapoor, 2005; Foley et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: BubR1Δ432–484, which cannot interact with Bub1 and localize to kinetochores, has a strong defect in kinetochore–microtubule attachment that correlates with a defective interaction with PP2AB56.
source: Our results demonstrate that BubR1Δ432–484, which cannot interact with Bub1 and localize to kinetochores, has a strong defect in kinetochore–microtubule attachment that correlates with a defective interaction with PP2AB56.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section based on the data in Figure 7D-E.

claim: Mad1/C-Mad2 at kinetochores acts as a template for the establishment of the Cdc20/C–Mad2 interaction.
source: We and others have previously shown that two conformers of Mad2, O-Mad2 and C-Mad2, form an asymmetric conformational dimer (Luo et al., 2004; De Antoni et al., 2005). In this reaction, Mad1 acts as a stable placeholder for C-Mad2 (De Antoni et al., 2005). Once at kinetochores, the Mad1/C-Mad2 complex recruits a high-turnover cytosolic form of O-Mad2 and converts it into the active C-Mad2 form, which targets Cdc20, thus overcoming a rate-limiting step towards the formation of MCC (De Antoni et al., 2005; Mapelli et al., 2007; Simonetta et al., 2009). This scheme, summarized in Figure 8B, identifies Mad1/Mad2 as a 'template' for the establishment of the Cdc20/C-Mad2 complex, a structural 'copy' of the Mad1/Mad2 complex (De Antoni et al., 2005; Musacchio and Salmon, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations and illustrated in Figure 8B.

claim: The MCC, made of Cdc20/C-Mad2 and BubR1/Bub3, can be interpreted as a 'copy' of kinetochore-bound 'templates' made of Mad1/C-Mad2 and Bub1/Bub3 complexes.
source: The MCC, made of Cdc20/C-Mad2 and BubR1/Bub3, can be interpreted as a 'copy' of kinetochore-bound 'templates' made of Mad1/C-Mad2 and Bub1/Bub3 complexes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the findings.
